arguments.query: register as a data controller threshold employees

turns.text: I have the registration sections. Pulling the full text of the two that decide this.

Yes, on this corpus you would need to register.

Registration is triggered by any one of three things, and you meet at least two of them: more than ten employees, turnover above the illustrative threshold, or processing personal data as a core part of what you do (DOC-DPA-01#S1). You have 14 employees, and holding customer names, phone numbers and delivery addresses in order to fulfil orders is core processing rather than incidental.

What it involves: you register as a data controller with the commissioner's office, the certificate runs for 24 months, and you renew it rather than registering again (DOC-DPA-01#S2). Registration is a filing, not an approval, so there is nothing to wait for before you continue trading.

Separately from registration, the controller duties apply to you anyway: keeping a record of what you process and why, answering a data subject request within 30 days, and reporting a personal data breach (DOC-DPA-01#S3, DOC-DPA-01#S4). Those are not conditional on being registered.

One thing to be clear about: this corpus is synthetic, written for a software demonstration, so treat the above as a worked example rather than legal advice.
